story_text.value:
https://giganticresearch.com

Yo whats up everyone? So let me drop right into it and not waste your time if you are reading this. I instantly grew a dislike for arXiv when I spent days writing up a research paper and then came to find out I need an endorsement to post at all. No pun intended, I should have done research but it was a slap in the face, especially since that same paper was accepted to ICTAI 2026 by someone who did the research for fun, 0 financial backing, 0 institutional backing, 0 affiliation. Research shouldn't be gated like that. Research is research and I can't imagine the amount of good, ground breaking research from everyday people that never sees the light of day because of this. Sure there is Zenodo, but you still have enough options to tell your lifes story which certainly effects viewership. And they have their own gates mechanism which is communities, want to post to a specific community where your audience is present? hold on there buster, needs to be reviewed before you can post. So i thought to myself, this is dumb, research is research and there should be a place for just that. and that might exist but I wanted to make my own version of it. So I did, giganticresearch.com. Its aim isn't to compete, its aim is to aggregate research from anyone who has something they want to share, no preferential treatment, the only research on display is the most recently uploaded research. You want your research shown? upload more! you want one of my 7 tiered badges that mean absolutely nothing but a cool little something next to your name that shows how much you've contributed? then make an account! and here is the wonderful part, you dont need to make an account to upload, anonymous is the default. I store 0 data on where it came from. The only thing an account does is ties you to the research, gets you a badge that means nothing really, and the ability to show you what you've uploaded and what you have favorited. The option to delete your account is there as well, and all the research you uploaded if you choose that option. Anon uploads stay uploaded. I wouldn't have a way to track an anon upload anyway because I store no data but the upload itself and the sha 256 tied to that research. There are two hard no go research topics that I will not allow to be uploaded, and you can read about on the About page. Other than that, push it, thats the point. I want us to have a research depot where you can find just about anything. Big or small. And it doesnt need to be YOUR research, it can be any research you want to share, on pretty much any topic you want to share. Also I implemented a forum, where anon is the default too, but feel free to use your account if you want there as well. The account is also just there to give you a handle to go by. No data is stored on that either in terms of identifying you. The anon part isn't there to be evasive per se, its also there because in this day and age, it seems privacy is less and less a thing, so if I can provide that in some way, then I will. I've been trying to promote this all day and I haven't had one person upload anything. It is just some of my research that I used to seed the site a little bit and thats it. So if any of this sounds interesting to anyone reading it and if you have any research you would like to share, if you could take a few mins and upload to my website I'd appreciate that and I thank you in advance my friend. I made the site as frictionless as possible, time is the only currency that matters in this world, the most valuable currency and the one currency we can not acquire more of, and I value your time so I made sure to make the process take up as little of it as possible. Again, I thank you for reading this even if you dont upload anything, and I double thank you if you do, either way, you get a thank you from me.

title.value: Show HN: Gigantic Research, Friend

story_text.value:
MaskShift is a local-first coding agent harness. Features:

- Works with models that have no tool-calling API. Tool schemas are rendered into the system prompt and the model calls them by writing a block in its reply, parsed back into a normal tool call.

- No npm runtime dependencies. Daemon are Node 22 built-ins only. Install is a file copy and a symlink.

- Multi-provider: Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, LM Studio, vLLM.

- 148 native tools: filesystem, shell, search/indexing, Git and Workspace, LSP, browser/CDP, containers, SSH, databases, web fetch.

- Lazy MCP loading. Catalog is searched, the relevant server connects on demand, only those tools enter the context window.

- 36 bundled skills, plus skills imported from Claude, Codex, and Copilot directories.

- Bridges to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, and Aider when they're on PATH.

- Scheduled automations, plugins, persistent memory, parallel agents in isolated worktrees.

- Web cockpit with live run telemetry, plan pane, tool traces, source browser, and a host terminal.

Permissive by default. No per-command approval. Recovery is pre-run checkpoints, Git stash refs, and an append-only audit log. Keep it on loopback or in the container.

title.value: Show HN: MaskShift – a maximalist coding agent with zero NPM dependencies

story_text.value:
I built VODForge because I work with a CTV company that needed to pull YouTube videos from our channel partners into our media workflow.

Converter sites are always an option but the bitrate wasn't optimal for a CTV network that needs to make multiple streaming version off of a single source file. So I build vodforge to use yt-dlp and ffmpeg under the hood with preconfigured settings for the highest quality end result, automatically adjusting the output settings based on source quality, frame rate, and things like that.

It became a game changer internally for us because we were able to avoid sketchy converter sites and avoid paid converter software. Eventually I decided to release it for free and others loved it as well. We started to add support for many of the features that other software charges for, supporting 4K, playlist support, customizing application theme, persistent searchable library, auto organizing downloads by channel and playlist, MP3 support up to 320 kbps, and much more.

Looking for feedback on the user experience and additional features that you might find useful. My goal is to grow VODForge into a widely adopted free tool for people who do not want to deal with sketchy websites, CLI mess, or pay for things that you could ultimately do for free given time and effort. VODForge wants to make it EASY and maintained for you. We know anyone can make a GUI wrapper, but that is a trivial way to describe what VODForge aims to offer, user-friendliness, "it just works", libraries and packages maintained for you. All you should think about is what to download next.

VODForge awaits...

story_text.value:
Double-click or press N to start a new experiment.

I built hexBOTs, an unusual cellular automaton based on deterministic robots.

The robots behave a bit like robotic lawnmowers, moving through their environment and reacting according to their individual rules.

The robots themselves are fully deterministic — no random functions are used while they are running. What makes them different is their “genetics”: each robot's behavior is defined by a randomly generated genome, which allows for an enormous number of different robot types.

Randomness creates the robots, but it doesn't drive them.

Once an experiment starts, everything follows deterministically from the generated genomes and the initial state. What fascinates me is the complexity that emerges from these relatively simple machines interacting with each other and their environment.

Controls:

B — enable/disable robots (also: hold mouse/finger down)

R — restart

N — new experiment (also: mouse/finger double-click)

D — save as picture

I — show information / controls

title.value: Show HN: HexBOTs – a cellular automaton with robotic lawnmowers

story_text.value:
I got tired of trying to go backpacking and losing out on permits either through lottery or someone effectively bid-sniping cancellations. So, I built a real-time alert system across every state and federal booking system in the US. This covers ~700 permitted trails and locations as well as campsites.

It's the first real end-to-end product I've ever built myself and I gotta say, it's a lot of fun. I had to build a ton of custom infra and adapters to connect to the various, disparate booking systems in order to find cancellation.

Definitely pushed my capabilities.

Hope this helps some of you finally land a trip you've been wanting to take.

Edit: I've created a forecast model for openings which has been quite accurate at a 7 and 14-day timespan. Next year I should be able to make this the backbone for predictive alerts. https://permitsnag.com/permit-forecasts

title.value: Show HN: Get hard to get backcountry permit

Hashem, skriin ai TV founder
